parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is a criminalising state with documented state torture, psychiatric confinement and impunity. Article 135 reaches a trans visitor through birth-sex reading of documents (trans woman plus male partner, or trans man read as two men), with the 2022 code increasing severity and scope. Enforcement has risen since 2006; suspects face interrogation, torture and mental-hospital confinement, and security services abuse with impunity. No trans legal category, no anti-discrimination law (rejected across three UN cycles), no civil society, state-only media, and no documented remedy. Asylum grants confirm persecution. Entry practice for trans people is undocumented — an open question, not a safety. Absent documented execution or routine visitor arrests keeps this just above the 0.15 tier.

entry_documents.exposure: No legal gender recognition exists; documents record birth sex. Authorities read trans status through that record, placing a trans woman or trans man within Article 135's scope in any relationship read as male-male.
entry_documents.interaction: Document sex marker → relationship construed as sodomy → criminal investigation → torture risk in custody.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Article 135 suspects face interrogation, torture, grossly humiliating questioning and confinement to mental hospitals; torture and inhuman treatment documented as present throughout the country with LGBTI victims.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No civil society, state-owned media only, corruption with impunity.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any outing or suspicion triggers the investigative apparatus; prison adds vigilante attacks.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Compulsory psychiatric admission and involuntary conversion therapy on repeat convictions; facilities treat homosexuality as mental disorder. Prison vigilante attacks especially common.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Detention converts criminal suspicion into institutionalised harm with no external oversight.

care_services.exposure: No trans-specific healthcare findings; psychiatric facilities are a harm channel, not care. HIV/LGBT people documented as lacking effective legislative means to rights.
care_services.interaction: Seeking care can route a trans visitor into the psychiatric-confinement pathway.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Government told a UN body that deviation from tradition poses a potential threat to society; anti-discrimination legislation rejected across three review cycles; 2022 code broadened and hardened penalties.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: A 2021 stated intention to 'study' anti-discrimination law — no legislative step sourced.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing licenses security-service abuse and forecloses legislative remedy.

minors_guardians.exposure: No youth- or minor-specific findings. A travelling minor shares the parent's exposure: birth-sex documents, no recognition framework, and the same investigative apparatus if the family is read as same-sex.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family composition read through birth sex can convert ordinary travel into an Article 135 suspicion.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State-sponsored violence and torture documented; vigilante attacks common in prison; security officials commit abuses with impunity. 2019 prolonged torture of a gay doctor; May 2020 arrests of public figures on homosexuality charges.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Impunity removes any deterrent between hostility and harm once a trans person is identified.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law, no legal recognition, no civil society, entirely state-owned media — incident frequency unverifiable. Asylum grants (2007, 2019) document that people flee persecution including imprisonment and torture.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Exit is the only documented remedy, confirming failed internal recourse.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: custody abuse, coerced interrogation and illusory remedies match. Lower than 0.15-A only because no credible capital pathway is documented and routine visitor arrests for presentation are not sourced here — hence slightly above rather than at 0.15.

Materially lower. That anchor's harm is exclusion and humiliation without arrest; here the documented consequence of discovery is criminal investigation with torture, psychiatric confinement and impunity — a full tier of severity below administrative exclusion.

Materially lower. That anchor has birth-sex facility placement plus a cross-dressing offence with slow remedies but no documented torture. This dossier documents state torture during investigation and psychiatric detention as routine outcomes.

Far lower. That anchor is discretionary secondary screening ending in refusal of entry; here the outcome after discovery is prosecution under an actively enforced statute whose suspects are tortured in custody.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is one system: birth-sex documents with no recognition mechanism feed an actively enforced sodomy statute whose 2022 iteration hardened penalties; suspicion then routes into an investigative apparatus documented to torture, humiliate and confine to psychiatric wards, with security-service impunity, no anti-discrimination law, no civil society and no independent media. Official threat-framing of deviation as a societal danger corroborates rather than offsets the enforcement record. The only documented remedies are asylum abroad. What keeps this marginally above the 0.15 tier is narrow: no execution pathway, no sourced routine arrests of trans visitors specifically, and entry-stage administrative practice unverified — an open question, not a protection.
